nodes.name: Impregnation-Pyrolysis Decoration
nodes.procedure: An easy-to-scale-up impregnation-pyrolysis strategy was designed to anchor Cu-O functional groups at the surface of NiCoS NAs, which can facilitate the removal of lattice anionic ligands (Sδ-) and promote the LOM catalysis of seawater oxygen evolution. The precursor concentration of 7 gL⁻¹ for impregnation-pyrolysis was applied.
nodes.source_text: Subsequently, an easy-to-scale-up impregnation-pyrolysis strategy was designed to anchor Cu-O functional groups at the surface of NiCoS NAs... Hence, the precursor concentration of 7gL⁻¹ for impregnation-pyrolysis was applied to prepare the CuO@NiCoS NAs/NF in subsequent studies.

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM images show well-defined heterointerface between CuO (d = 0.253 nm) and NiCo2S4 (d = 0.332 nm).
nodes.evidence_snippet: In Figure 2a, highresolution transmission electron microscopy (HRTEM) images of Cu2+/1+ cation substituents anchored NiCoS NAs showed a well-defined heterointerface between the found CuO (d = 0.253 nm) and NiCo2S4 d = 0.332nm).

nodes.characterization_summary: PXRD pattern of initial NiCoS NAs/NF indexed to NiCo2S4 (ICDD 20-0782) and NiS (ICDD 08-8457); CuO@NiCoS NAs/NF shows diffraction peaks indexed to CuO (ICDD 80-1916) and Cu2O (ICDD 20-7578) in enlarged pattern (Figure S3).
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure 2b, the powder X-ray diffraction (PXRD) pattern of the initial NiCoS NAs/NF was indexed to the International Centre for Diffraction Data (ICDD) card No. 200782 (NiCo2S4) and card No. 088457 (NiS) for reference... In addition, the diffraction peaks indexed to CuO (ICDD card No. 801916) and Cu2O (ICDD card No. 207578) in the enlarged PXRD pattern of CuO@NiCoS NAs/NF (Figure S3, Supporting Information).

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM images of CuO@NiCoS NAs show film-like morphology of deposited Cu-O groups at well-distributed NiCoS NAs on nickel substrate (Figure S4).
nodes.evidence_snippet: Besides, the scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and energy dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) images of CuO@NiCoS NAs (Figure S4, Supporting Information) unveiled the film-like morphology of deposited Cu-O groups, which are located at the geometric structure of well-distributed NiCoS NAs on the nickel substrate.

nodes.characterization_summary: TOF-SIMS 3D mapping shows distinct Cu-component species signal intensity on CuO@NiCoS NAs surface with homogeneous distribution overlaying hybrid transition metal sulfides.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The depth profiling analysis of the TOF-SIMS 3D render in Figure 2i revealed that the surface of CuO@NiCoS NAs heterostructure displayed a distinct signal intensity of Cu-component species.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS shows Cu 2p peaks at 933.5/953.09 eV (Cu(II)) and 932.23/952.05 eV (Cu(I)); negative shifts in O 1s (529.9→529.6 eV), S 2p, Ni 2p (855.3→854.6 eV, 872.9→872.3 eV), Co 2p peaks; increased surface sulfate at 168.0 eV.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Instead of the single Cu-O groups, the Cu2p high-resolution XPS spectrum of CuO@NiCoS NAs exhibited two couples of minimum binding energy (BE) spin-orbit peaks at 933.5 eV (Cu 2p3/2) & 953.09 eV (Cu 2p1/2), and 932.23 eV (Cu 2p3/2) & 952.05 eV (Cu 2p1/2).

nodes.characterization_summary: UPS shows work function of CuO@NiCoS NAs (7 gL⁻¹) at 5.08 eV, higher than NiCoS NAs (4.26 eV).
nodes.evidence_snippet: Notably, the probed work function of CuO@NiCoS NAs (7gL⁻¹) is 5.08 eV, which is noticeably higher than the value of single NiCoS NAs (4.26 eV).

nodes.characterization_summary: Operando EC-Raman shows Ni(III)-O Eg (473 cm⁻¹) and A1g (552 cm⁻¹) modes at 1.34 V vs RHE for CuO@NiCoS NAs; increasing I_Eg/I_A1g ratio indicates amorphous γ-NiOOH formation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Ni(III)-O depolarized Eg mode (bending) at 473 cm⁻¹ and polarized A1g mode (stretching) at 552 cm⁻¹ of the CuO@NiCoS NAs were observed since the anodic potential reached 1.34 V vs RHE.

nodes.characterization_summary: Operando EC-FTIR shows Niᴵᴵ-O at ~941 cm⁻¹ (1.29 V), Niᴵᴵᴵ-O at 1003→1010 cm⁻¹, M-O-O-M at 1103 cm⁻¹ (1.29 V) for CuO@NiCoS NAs; faster transformation than NiCoS NAs.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The distinctive absorption peaks of Mδ+O-O-M+ intermediates (1103 cm⁻¹) presented at the constant potential of 1.29 V vs RHE after the decoration of low electronegativity Cu²⁺/¹⁺ cation substituents.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS confirms elemental composition of CuO@NiCoS NAs alongside SEM imaging (Figure S4).
nodes.evidence_snippet: Besides, the scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and energy dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) images of CuO@NiCoS NAs (Figure S4, Supporting Information) unveiled the film-like morphology of deposited Cu-O groups.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRF shows Cu content increasing from 0.43 wt.% (0.40 at.%) at 3 gL⁻¹ to 0.92 wt.% (0.85 at.%) at 7 gL⁻¹ Cu(NO3)2 precursor, and 1.32 wt.% (1.22 at.%) at 11 gL⁻¹ (Table S2).
nodes.evidence_snippet: As the concentration of the Cu(NO3)2 precursor solution for the impregnation-pyrolysis procedure increased from 3 to 7 gL⁻¹, the X-ray Fluorescence Spectrometer (XRF) weight and atom quantifications of Cu-metal element were increased from 0.43 wt.% and 0.40 at.% to 0.92 wt.% and 0.85 at.%, respectively (Table S2, Supporting Information).
